newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil high court has no more CVRD cases, for now.
newsitem.headline: Brazil high court has no more CVRD cases, for now.

text.p: Brazil's highest court, the Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF), has no more cases requesting injunctions against the privatization of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), a judge said.

STF Judge Marco Aurelio de Mello said he did not rule out the possibility of further cases against the sell-off being lodged either before or after the April 29 auction of 45 percent of CVRD's voting shares.
"That's it for the time being," Mello told reporters.
The STF earlier Monday rejected two cases brought against the sale, one by the Order of Brazilian Lawyers (OAB) and the other by a left-wing party.
Mello noted that the court had only ruled on the merit of the injunctions and not on the merit of the cases themselves.

He said the STF was due to vote Wednesday on the constitutionality of the 1991 privatization of steel mill Usiminas. The STF rejected the injunction sought in 1990 but had still to rule on the merit of the case, Mello said.
Mello said he would vote against the case but if the other judges disagreed and decided the sale was unconstitutional, every privatization since 1990 would be reversed.
"This could hurl the country into chaos," Mello said.
While the STF had for now cleared its desks of CVRD cases, other lower courts around the country were studying up to 100 applications for injunctions.
By late afternoon, four regional courts had granted six different injunctions, suspending the auction. In Sao Paulo, a judge rejected a government appeal against one of the injunctions.
Government officials say they are confident they can get the injunctions revoked in time for the sale to begin Tuesday.
